_meta.notes: The version now lives in index.html, in a meta tag, because that is the one file a reload always refetches. This file mirrors it so the app can say when a device is running a part cached page, and it carries the notes a student reads. Bump both together: the sweep fails if they disagree. Entries are for the person using it: what is different on their screen, never what changed in the code.

releases.head: What it costs, and what help there is
changes: A new page about money. What every route costs a Singapore Citizen before any help, then nine kinds of help by name, then four things that are true whatever the numbers say.

The names are the point. MOE Financial Assistance, Edusave, the Post Secondary Education Account, bursaries at ITE and poly and university, the Tuition Fee Loan, the CPF Education Scheme, CDAC and MENDAKI and SINDA and the Eurasian Association, my school's own welfare fund, and SkillsFuture later. Almost none of it is offered. All of it has to be asked for.

Every route in Plan now shows what it costs right there on the card, so nobody has to go looking. A route with no number beside it is a silence a family fills with a guess, and the guess is always too high.
The parent page leads with the money question, because it is the first thing a parent asks.
Every figure says Not yet verified, in the same words the admission bars use. Fee schedules change every year and a precise wrong number is worse than an honest range.
The whole page prints on paper, so it can go to a general office with the scheme names already on it.

releases.head: The other half: what the work actually is
changes: There is a whole new page about work. Sixteen parts of working Singapore, from building and care to computing and the arts, each one with what the job actually is, what a day holds, where the work is heading, and what people get wrong about it.

Every single one of those sixteen takes people in at three or more levels: from ITE, from a polytechnic, from a university, sometimes from an arts school. That is the point of the page and it is true.

What a first job pays is stated once, for each level of entry, and never per sector. Comparing sectors on pay is a ranking in disguise, and the spread inside a level is wider than the gap between levels anyway.
Naming a want in Act now shows the parts of working life that turn on it. Saying I honestly do not know yet shows one from each of the six kinds, because not knowing is the reason to look.
Every subject now says where it turns up in working life. Tap a subject in Plan and the answer to why am I learning this is right there.

That fix caught something worse. The G1 syllabus subjects named no work at all while the G3 ones named six, from the same screen, about the same subject. Every subject anybody can take now reaches at least two parts of working life, and the app refuses to build if one does not.

releases.head: The people in it belong where I am
changes: Nobody offers me a Year Head in a polytechnic any more. Polys and ITEs have lecturers, course managers and a career centre; JCs have Year Heads; secondary schools have form teachers. Every option down the side and every option straight down is now one that exists where I am standing.

The card that turns up between years has to make sense. The lab technician now notices a term of staying back to redo the practical, not two titrations, and what he offers is the name of whoever runs the Science team.

Putting real hours into a subject counts later. Going to remedial, finding somewhere to actually study, going deeper into my best subject: any of those and the A Level year, the first semester, the workshop routine and the studio brief all read differently when I get there.
A replay is a different year. One card used to take almost two thirds of everything dealt in some chapters; now no card takes more than a quarter, so playing again is playing something new.

Six new cards for the JC and Millennia years: the Project Work group where two people have not read the brief, four H2 or three, the diploma course I actually want, council in the year the papers get real, the Mother Tongue paper I keep postponing, and the H3 letter.
Sixty two lines of broken English fixed, including fourteen sentences where the word I was doing the job of me.
A polytechnic will not hold an offer for a year so I can earn, the SkillsFuture top up arrives at forty and not before, and there is no shortcut from poly to SMU. All three said otherwise.

releases.head: The game talks the way I would
changes: Every choice and every outcome is in my own words now. It says my best subject and my Early Admissions folder, not yours.
The options say what they actually mean. Guard your own oxygen is gone, and so is Keep one made thing alive.
The things that fill a real school year are in: class comm, CCA EXCO, the Sec 3 immersion trip, a programme outside school, leading a VIA project, tutoring somebody younger.
Some choices now pay off for the rest of the game. Build a study routine and every year after it gives me one more point.
CCA, VIA, PW, EXCO, DSA, ORD and NYAA are all in Words now, so anyone can look them up.
The button at the end of a year says That is my year.
On a phone, the button that starts the game and the button that ends a year are where a thumb can reach them. They were off the bottom of the screen.
The version is printed at the bottom of every page, so a teacher can check the class is on the same one.

releases.head: This is version 2
changes: The game plays in chapters now: school year by year, then the milestones that actually shape the years after, National Service included if it is part of your road.
Every figure that could be checked against MOE has been, and the ones that could not still say so.
The list of places never changes order. It never did rank you, and now it cannot.
Your class code now means what your teacher says it means.
A landing page that asks you one question before anything else.
